thread_field_definitions.base_priority: Base priority reported by THREADENTRY32, in Windows priority levels.
thread_field_definitions.current_priority: Relative thread priority returned by GetThreadPriority; this is not a guaranteed instantaneous scheduler priority.
thread_field_definitions.creation_time_utc: Thread creation timestamp converted from Windows FILETIME to UTC.
thread_field_definitions.user_cpu_time_seconds: Cumulative thread CPU time in user mode, in seconds.
thread_field_definitions.kernel_cpu_time_seconds: Cumulative thread CPU time in kernel mode, in seconds.
thread_field_definitions.owning_process_name: Process name joined by owner_process_id from the separate process snapshot.

not_collected_fields.thread_state: Not collected: the selected documented Toolhelp and thread timing APIs do not provide a supported thread-state inventory.
not_collected_fields.wait_reason: Not collected: determining wait reason requires a system-information interface outside the documented APIs used by this collector.
not_collected_fields.start_address: Not collected: this collector does not use undocumented thread information classes to query a start address.
not_collected_fields.context_switch_count: Not collected: per-thread context-switch counters are not provided by the documented APIs used by this collector.

limitations: This is a point-in-time system-wide thread inventory; threads can start or exit during collection.
Current-priority, creation-time, and CPU-time fields are best-effort queries and can be denied or fail if a thread exits during collection.
Unavailable thread values are null; reasons and affected counts are summarized in collection_errors rather than repeated in each thread record.
CPU time is cumulative and is not an instantaneous utilization measurement.
The Toolhelp snapshot does not identify whether a thread is executing in user mode or kernel mode.
This output is not a separate inventory of kernel-only processes or kernel-mode threads.
